title: The discounted dividend measure on a finite set of active payment times is bounded by the sum of the discounted verification-value drops, under the two separate generator and gradient inequalities
author: @WillR
source: The separated-hypothesis variant of the Proved theorem local_verification_capped_finset_dividendMeasure_bound, which assumes the HJB equality max (X.generator w y - q * w y) (1 - deriv w y) = 0. The two separate inequalities X.generator w y - q * w y ≤ 0 and 1 ≤ deriv w y imply only that the maximum is nonpositive, so the HJB form is not available to the target local_verification_separated_countable_dividend_budget, whose hypotheses are the separate ones. That target is the countable budget of the local verification argument, and its proof applies the finite budget to the finitely many jump times below each index of an enumeration of the countable set of active payment times and then passes to the limit, so it needs this finite budget in the separated form. This is the finite counterpart of the Proved theorem local_verification_capped_countable_dividendMeasure_bound_separated, which gives the same comparison on a countable set of times.

title: The dividend measure is carried by the countable set of right jumps when it has no continuous part on the non-negative half-line
author: @WillR
source: The non-negative-range variant of the published theorem dividendMeasure_countable_rightJump_concentration_of_purely_atomic. The measure of an interval (a, b] for the dividend measure is the increase of the right limit of the dividend path, which decomposes into the sum of the right jumps of that path in the interval plus a continuous part; the hypothesis hatomic is the assumption that the continuous part vanishes. Together with the Proved countability of the right-jump set, dividendStrategy_countable_rightJump_times, this makes the dividend measure carried by a countable set, which is what allows a countable budget for the discounted dividends to bound the dividend measure of a dividend strategy. The restriction 0 <= a is what the unbounded-variation stochastic core needs, since the right-jump set of the dividend path is contained in the non-negative half-line, and it avoids asking for the statement on intervals that reach below the origin, where the right limit of the dividend path at the origin need not vanish for a general dividend strategy.

title: The Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure of a dividend strategy without a continuous part is carried by the countable set of its right jumps
author: @WillR
source: The corrected countable right-jump concentration statement for the Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure of a dividend strategy. The measure of an interval (a, b] for the dividend measure is the increase of the right limit of the dividend path, which decomposes into the sum of the right jumps of that path in the interval plus a continuous part; the hypothesis hatomic is the assumption that the continuous part vanishes. Together with the Proved countability of the right-jump set, dividendStrategy_countable_rightJump_times, this makes the dividend measure carried by a countable set, which is what allows a countable budget for the discounted dividends to bound the dividend measure of a dividend strategy. This supersedes the earlier statement dividendMeasure_countable_rightJump_concentration, which omitted the no-continuous-part hypothesis and is therefore false for a general dividend strategy.

title: Affine sections and localization of a finite-rank locally free sheaf
author: @tomasz
source: Consequence of Stacks Project, Section 26.7, especially Lemma 26.7.4 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I6), and Lemma 10.78.2, equivalences (2), (6), (7) (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NX). A finite-rank locally free sheaf is quasi-coherent. On any affine open it is associated with its module of sections, which is finite projective and hence finitely generated. The principal-open localization comparison in Section 26.7 gives the two displayed formal localization conditions. This is the concrete affine-section consequence in the existing OModulePresheaf interface, rather than a verbatim transcription. No Noetherian assumption is needed.

Nombres Bordeaux 16 (2004), 535–553, Théorème 2, and in Diaz 2007, Théorème 4(1). source: Derived consequence of componentwise normalization of proper curves and projectivity of proper regular curves: Stacks Project, Lemma 53.2.9(1) and its normalization argument, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BY4 , and the componentwise treatment of geometric curves in Section 53.18, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CE0 . The algebraic base-change dimension bound uses stability of integral morphisms under base change and their dimension inequality, Lemmas 29.45.6 and 29.45.9, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01WG . This formulation includes reducible, nonreduced and empty proper schemes via the finite disjoint union of smooth projective covers of their reduced irreducible components. title: A five-dimensional space of rational functions of u containing 1, u, u⁻¹ carries a 2×3 configuration iff it is D1, D2a or D2b
author: @carlok
source: Not found in the sources read: the “only if” half, the classification. Applied to conjugation hulls (with DiazModulus.rational_conj_hull_le_adjoin) it gives the five-dimensional case of Theorem F (DiazModulus.rational_conj_hull_two_by_three_configuration_iff). Theorem F asks the question of Theorem E of the mission's research note on polynomial and Laurent hulls (DiazModulus.laurent_conj_hull_two_by_three_configuration_iff, Laurent z) for every z rational in u, and builds on Theorem B (DiazModulus.circle_point_extension_two_by_three_configuration_iff, 10.6), which holds for every complex z. For Laurent z, agreement with Theorem E's classes was checked by exact computation, not proved. Its configurations give, at a candidate, exclusions that are substitutions in Roy's strong six exponentials theorem (D. Roy, Matrices whose coefficients are linear forms in logarithms, J. Number Theory 41 (1992), 22–47, Cor. 2). Uses DiazModulus.degree_two_configuration_normal_form, DiazModulus.quadratic_two_orbit_space_carries_two_by_three_configuration, DiazModulus.quadratic_cyclic_space_carries_two_by_three_configuration, DiazModulus.rational_space_configuration_coprime_ratio, DiazModulus.mobius_ratio_configuration_u_multiplier_triple and DiazModulus.two_by_three_configuration_ratio_degree_le_two. R20 of the Diaz modulus mission. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 23 October 2026 (C. Perassi).
